videos.title: How To Stand Out In A World Of AI Designs
videos.description:
Magic Patterns (W23) is one of the fastest-growing design tools in AI, helping product teams turn ideas into interactive, code-backed prototypes in minutes.

Alex Danilowicz and his co-founder, both front-end engineers, built 
Magic Patterns to solve a problem they had themselves: finding a better way to turn ideas into something visual. They were among the first teams building prompt-to-design tools back in 2023.

In this episode of Design Review, Alex joins YC’s Aaron Epstein to demo Magic Patterns and its new MagicOS canvas, where teams can bring together prompts, images, PRDs, and other context to explore ideas visually. Then they review a handful of startup websites to break down what makes a site feel “vibe coded,” where founders go wrong, and how to make AI-generated design feel more intentional.

videos.title: How to Deploy AI & LLMs with RunPod Serverless
videos.description:
Most developers don't need to OWN a GPU — they need one for the 90 seconds it takes to answer a request. In this video I sign up for RunPod live on camera, deploy FLUX.1-schnell as a serverless endpoint, and prove the whole story with real numbers:

▶️ Sign up to a working AI endpoint — no sales calls, no contracts
▶️ What a cold start actually looks like (worker boots from zero)
▶️ The FlashBoot difference: 13-minute cold start → 131ms warm response
▶️ Firing 20 concurrent requests and watching the worker pool scale
▶️ The final bill — pennies per image, exactly $0 when idle

Everything I demo is reproducible from the public repo, including the notebook: https://github.com/sourangshupal/runpod-serverless-demo

➡️ Ready to try it yourself? Sign up here: https://fandf.co/4xaI3kV 

First thing to do after signing up: create an API key (Settings → API Keys), deploy a serverless endpoint from the Hub, and send your first request — the whole path takes under 10 minutes.

In today’s episode, we sit down with Ayyoub “Ello” El Osrouti, Professional Athlete and Ultrarunner, to discuss how he went from barely running to competing at an elite level in just four years.

We discuss why he stopped after running over 620 km in a Backyard Ultra, how he trained his mind to tolerate extreme pain, and what he learned from David Goggins about discipline, mental toughness, and pushing beyond his limits. Ello breaks down his 7-day training routine, what he eats during a 93-hour race, the supplements he takes for recovery, and how he balances physical limitations with his drive to keep going.

The conversation also explores how he deals with the urge to quit, why he focuses on one loop at a time instead of the total distance, how visualization helped shape his ambitions, and his practical advice for anyone looking to build mental strength, get out of their comfort zone, and change their life.

videos.title: The Difference Between Chemistry & Compatibility Nobody Explains | Quinlan Walther
videos.description:
Don't go grocery shopping when you're starving.
You grab the first thing you see.
You grab what looks exciting, not what you need.
Quinlan Walther says dating works the same way.

In this episode, Quinlan Walther and Jay Shetty talk about the difference between wanting love and being ready for it.

Quinlan shares four steps to trusting yourself. She explains why you don't have to be perfect before you meet someone, and why love as a feeling is never enough.

She opens up about the time she lost herself chasing someone to choose her, and she shares what her mom's final months taught her.

Learn why the spark can fool you. And learn why Quinlan says you can't hold your partner accountable.
